newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends sharply down on bank probe.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends sharply down on bank probe.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index dropped sharply on Monday after a leading A share firm postponed a shareholders' meeting due to a probe into share trading irregularities, analysts said.
The foreign currency B share index plummeted 6.85 points or 4.47 percent to 146.34 as turnover inflated to HK$263.5 million from HK$99 million on Friday.

The Shenzhen Development Bank, a large capitalisation firm in the local currency A share market, on Monday said it would defer the shareholders' meeting pending an investigation into trading irregularities.
The statement gave no details and bank officials declined to elaborate.
"The Shenzhen Bank's failure to conduct a shareholders' meeting sent bad vibes to the market," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Investors are very sensitive after many of the recent rumours concerning the market clampdown were proved to be true," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
The government began to dish out measures to cool stock trading around the start of May after share prices had risen more than 50 percent in the first four months of this year.

Beijing recently said it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading and increased the share supply with a 30 billion yuan quota for new domestic share issues as part of measures to cool down the markets.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai exchanges in the last two weeks suspended trading in a number of A shares for investigations into possible irregularities.

The Shenzhen Bank's announcement had less effect on the domestic A share index, which receded from earlier heavy losses to end Monday down 1.48 points or 0.35 percent to 424.24 on turnover of 5.7 billion yuan, against Friday's 7.0 billion.
The B share market contains a larger proportion of Shenzhen-based companies compared with its A share conterpart, and was therefore harder hit, brokers said.
"Also, A share investors tend to take more risks and jumped in for bargain-hunting as soon as the Shenzhen bank shares steadied out," an analyst at a major domestic bank said.
Shenzhen Bank ended the day at 37.80 yuan, down 1.25 yuan or 3.2 percent, after hitting an intra-day low of 35.60 yuan.
